title: He Traded 10,000 Bitcoin For Two Pizzas
description:
In 2010, a programmer paid 10,000 Bitcoin for two pizzas -- the first real-world purchase ever made with it. Here's what those coins would be worth today.

#shorts #financefacts #bitcoin #didyouknow

scenes.text: In May of 2010, a Florida programmer named Laszlo Hanyecz posted online offering ten thousand Bitcoin to anyone willing to order him two pizzas.
A nineteen year old on the same forum took him up on it, ordered two large Papa John's pizzas, and delivered them in exchange for the coins.
At the time, ten thousand Bitcoin was worth about forty one dollars. It was the first known real-world purchase ever made with it.
Bitcoin's price has moved a long way since then. As of one recent pricing snapshot, that same ten thousand coins would be worth well over seven hundred million dollars.
Hanyecz has said publicly, more than once, that he doesn't regret it -- somebody had to actually spend the stuff to prove it worked as real money.
Every year on May twenty second, the crypto world marks the anniversary as Bitcoin Pizza Day.
If you had ten thousand Bitcoin sitting untouched right now, would you actually be able to leave it alone?
